=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17403-17434 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The auto-reset state rewrite is not guarded, so post-reset labels, comments, notifications, and audit steps run even when `jq` or `mv` fails.
  WHY: A failed persistence write leaves the state in `failed` while consumer-facing surfaces claim a reset succeeded, causing state/label divergence and preventing reliable recovery.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17343-17358 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The manual `/re-security-pass` handler uses the same unguarded `jq ... && mv` pattern, allowing reset side effects after a failed state write.
  WHY: The handler can advertise a successful reset while the failed state and reset ledger remain unchanged.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17388-17434 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: An unreadable state file is converted to an empty engine SHA and treated as a different engine, allowing an unintended auto-reset attempt.
  WHY: Swallowed state-read errors permit reset processing against unverifiable state and compound the unguarded write failure path.

- agents.md:973-1014 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: New emitted log prefixes, including `SECURITY_PASS_AUTO_RESET`, `SECURITY_PASS_AUTO_RESET_SKIPPED`, `STAGED_SUPPORT_LATCH_RELEASED`, `STAGED_SUPPORT_LATCH_SKIP`, `STAGED_SUPPORT_LATCH_RELEASE_SKIPPED`, and `ORCHESTRATOR_ENGINE_SHA`, are not registered in the stable contractual prefix lists.
  WHY: Workflow-log-analysis and API-hygiene reporting depend on the registry, so these recovery and latch events remain invisible to periodic audit reports.

- README.md:1591 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Section 13 documents the obsolete `gh issue list --label ai:needs-human` transport and outdated consumer-repository API-cost behavior.
  WHY: Operators receive incorrect rate-limit and repository-scope information; severity was reported as both MAJOR and NIT, so the highest severity is used and the disagreement is noted.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  PROBLEM: The auto-reset state rewrite uses `jq ... > "${STATE_FILE}.tmp" && mv ...`, but the five post-reset steps execute unconditionally after the chain.
  WHY: If `jq` fails, the state remains terminal while labels and comments claim the reset succeeded, causing repeated failed retries and label/comment churn.

- agents.md: the LOG_PREFIX.name registry at lines 973-1014 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Five new contractual log prefixes are emitted but not registered in the stable-prefix registry.
  WHY: Workflow-log-analysis tooling will not classify or surface the new auto-reset and latch-release markers.

- README.md:1591 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Section 13 still documents the old `gh issue list --label ai:needs-human` transport and consumer-repository cost behavior.
  WHY: Operators may underestimate paginated REST API calls and misattribute which repositories incur the cost.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17418-17434 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3

  WHY: An unreadable state file can trigger an unintended reset attempt and unguarded post-reset side effects.

- README.md: line ~1591 (section 13 "Stall detection and self-healing", sentence starting "API cost: one `gh issue list --label ai:needs-human` per tick, plus 1 comments read, 1 label edit and 1 comment per released issue (consumer repos never set the staged-support ledger, so there the list is normally empty)") | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The staged-support sweep documentation names the old transport and obsolete consumer-repository cost model.
  WHY: Operators budgeting rate-limit spend or auditing API calls will see behavior that no longer matches the source-repository-only paginated REST implementation.

- agents.md: the `## Stable log prefixes (contractual)` section, the `LOG_PREFIX.name=…` machine-readable list near the end of that section (the existing entries above `SECURITY_PASS_*` around the `SECURITY_PASS_CLEAN`/`SECURITY_PASS_BLOCKED` rows) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Four new contractual prefixes, plus the per-issue `STAGED_SUPPORT_LATCH_SKIP` variant, are absent from the machine-readable registry.
  WHY: Reporting keyed to the registry will not classify the new auto-reset and latch-release markers.
